page: Microsoft Azure E32-8ds_v6 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the Edsv6 family. It is equipped with an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz, featuring 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. The system is provisioned with 256.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 32.0 GB per core. It includes 1890 GB of local storage and supports Premium Storage, operating under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2051.0 and a Geekbench text processing score of 2687.0, both placing in the top 25%. For lightweight language model tasks, it achieves a strong text generation speed of 320.89 tokens per second using a small 135M model. However, memory performance presents a tradeoff; the Passmark memory score of 1716.72 is in the bottom 25%, and text generation for a medium 7B model drops to a weak 8.29 tokens per second. Most other workloads, including multi-core CPU tasks, static web serving, and Redis operations, perform in the average range.

Given its massive memory allocation of 256.0 GB relative to its 8 vCPUs, this server offers high resource density for memory-bound workloads without requiring the expense of scaling up vCPU counts. The inclusion of 1890 GB of local storage makes it highly suitable for memory-intensive databases, caching layers, and data processing pipelines that require substantial local scratch space but do not demand extreme multi-core parallelization.
